'''GB Railfreight''' (GBRf) is a rail freight company in the United Kingdom. As of 2022, it is owned by the global investment company [[M&G|Infracapital]], itself a subsidiary of M&G plc, a UK investment group.

GB Railfreight was established in April 1999 as the rail freight operating subsidiary of the train operating company [[GB Railways]]. It was granted an operator's licence in June 2000, and started running [[intermodal freight transport|Intermodal container]] trains in February 2002; the haulage of other freight traffic commenced later that year. GBRf acquired numerous [[British Rail Class 66|Class 66]] locomotives to haul its trains; another early type would be the [[British Rail Class 20|Class 20]] and [[British Rail Class 73|Class 73]] locomotives. In August 2003, GBRf, via its parent company GB Railways, was acquired by [[FirstGroup]]; it was later rebranded as ''First GBRf''. In 2005, it began running services for [[Royal Mail]] and [[Metronet (British infrastructure company)|Metronet]]; two years later, First GBRf ran its first coal trains. In 2009, it was granted a passenger license, after which it operated such services under contract to [[First Great Western]].

In June 2010, the company was acquired by [[Europorte]], after which the GB Railfreight branding and livery were promptly reinstated. Following this purchase, it took on Europorte's fleet of [[British Rail Class 92|Class 92]] electric locomotives, as well as buying additional Class 66s and [[British Rail Class 56|Class 56]]s amongst other types to expand its inventory as service volume rose. Contracts to haul new-build rolling stock for operators and operate rail traffic at multiple [[steelworks]] were awarded during the early 2010s; GBRf also begun operations on hauling the [[Caledonian Sleeper]] service in April 2015. During October 2016, the company was bought by [[EQT AB]], and was partly integrated with [[Hector Rail]]. In September 2019, GBRf's ownership changed hands again, this time to Infracapitial.

==History==
===Formation and launch===
[[File:Class 66 Diesel in special "Rainbow" livery.jpg|thumb|GBRf Class 66, "Pride of GB Railfeight" in rainbow livery, with a full load from Arcow Quarry, Ribblesdale]]
[[File:66724 FirstGBRf.jpg|thumb|[[British Rail Class 66|Class 66]] in First GBRf livery at [[Doncaster railway station|Doncaster station]] in September 2007]]
[[File:First gbrf logo.svg|thumb|First GBRf logo]]
The origins of GB Railfreight can be traced back to early 1999, when the privately owned train operating company [[GB Railways]] decided to form its own dedicated rail freight subsidiary.<ref>{{cite report |url = http://www.parliament.the-stationery-office.co.uk/pa/cm200304/cmselect/cmtran/145/145wec03.htm |title = Memorandum by GB Railfreight |work = Hansard |first = Michael |last = Schabas |date = October 2003 |access-date = 18 October 2012 |url-status = dead |archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20120819061351/http://www.parliament.the-stationery-office.co.uk/pa/cm200304/cmselect/cmtran/145/145wec03.htm |archive-date = 19 August 2012 |df = dmy }}</ref> Accordingly, unlike the majority of private rail freight companies that emerged in the British market during the 1990s, such as [[DB Cargo UK]] and [[Freightliner Group|Freightliner]], GB Railfreight was not formed from any element of the [[privatisation of British Rail|privatised British Rail]] freight sectors.

During April 2000, following the awarding of an eight-year contract to operate infrastructure trains on behalf of British railway infrastructure owner [[Railtrack]], the company ordered seven [[British Rail Class 66|Class 66]] locomotives.<ref>{{cite magazine |title = GBR orders 66 fleet for Railtrack contract |magazine = [[Rail Magazine]] |issue = 382 |date = 3 May 2000 |page = 5}}</ref><ref>{{cite magazine |title = GB Rail signs freight contract with Railtrack |magazine = [[The Railway Magazine]] |issue = 1190 |date = June 2000 |page = 10}}</ref> In June 2000, GB Railfreight was granted an operator's licence, permitted it to run trains on the British rail network.<ref>{{cite magazine |title = GB Railfreight given licence |magazine = [[Rail Magazine]]|issue = 388 |date = 26 July 2000 |page = 4}}</ref> On 1 April 2000, it commenced operations.<ref>{{cite magazine |title = GB Railfreight signs deal with West Coast Traincare |magazine = [[Rail Magazine]]|issue = 406 |date = 4 April 2001 |page = 13}}</ref> During February 2002, GBRf commenced operating its first [[intermodal freight transport|Intermodal container]] contract from the [[Port of Felixstowe]] for MSC Mendite.<ref>{{cite magazine |title = GBRf starts container service to Selby |magazine = [[The Railway Magazine]]|issue = 1212 |date = April 2002 |page = 95}}</ref> Also that same year, GBRf began its first bulk freight contract for [[BPB plc|British Gypsum]].<ref name=Rail609>{{cite magazine |title = Making sure the mail on rail doesn't fail |magazine = [[Rail Magazine]]|issue = 609 |date = 14 January 2009 |page = 50}}</ref>

===FirstGroup era===
During August 2003, GB Railways was purchased by the British transport conglomerate [[FirstGroup]]; subsequently, GB Railfreight was rebranded as ''First GBRf''.<ref>{{cite press release |url = http://www.firstgroup.com/latest_news/?id=003551 |title = GB Rail Offer Unconditional |publisher = FirstGroup plc |work = Corporate News |date = 14 August 2003 |access-date = 18 October 2012 |url-status = dead |archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20131004215148/http://www.firstgroup.com/latest_news/?id=003551 |archive-date = 4 October 2013 |df = dmy }}</ref><ref>{{cite magazine |title = First Group buys GB for $22million |magazine = [[The Railway Magazine]] |issue = 1229 |date = September 2003 |page = 10}}</ref><ref>{{cite magazine |title = GB Railways is bought by First Group for £22 million |magazine = [[Rail Express]] |issue = 88 |date = September 2003 |page = 8}}</ref> In April 2004, GB Railfreight commenced operating a five-year contract for [[Network Rail]]; it also expanded its fleet through the acquisition of four former [[Gatwick Express]] [[British Rail Class 73|Class 73]] locomotives and numerous additional wagons to work the new contract.<ref>{{cite magazine |title = Network Rail hands GBRf more work: Class 73s acquired, wagons bought |magazine = [[Rail Express]] |issue = 94 |date = March 2004 |page = 8}}</ref>

In May 2005, First GBRf began operating [[Royal Mail]] services using [[British Rail Class 325|Class 325]] electric multiple-units (EMUs).<ref>{{cite press release |url = http://www.gbrailfreight.com/news_archive.php?year=2004&newsid=69 |title = Mail to move by rail again |work = GB Railfreight News |date = 18 October 2004 |access-date = 18 October 2012 |archive-date = 26 February 2012 |archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20120226135706/http://www.gbrailfreight.com/news_archive.php?year=2004 |url-status = dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite magazine |title = Mail back on rail: GBRf wins postal contract |magazine = [[The Railway Magazine]] |issue = 1244 |date = December 2004 |page = 4}}</ref> The company's arrangement with Royal Mail was subsequently extended through to 2010.<ref>{{cite press release |url = http://www.gbrailfreight.com/news_archive.php?year=2005&newsid=116 |title = GB Railfreight wins Royal Mail contract |work = GB Railfreight News |date = 20 May dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite press release |url = http://www.gbrailfreight.com/news_archive.php?newspage=6&newsid=177 |title = FirstGBRf wins new contact (sic) with Royal Mail |work = GB Railfreight News |date = 15 June 2007 |access-date = 18 October 2012 |archive-date = 17 October 2014 |archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20141017113459/http://www.gbrailfreight.com/news_archive.php?newspage=6&newsid=177 |url-status = dead }}</ref> Also in 2005, GBRf commenced operating [[London Underground]] infrastructure trains for [[Metronet (British infrastructure company)|Metronet]].<ref name=Rail609/><ref>{{cite magazine |title = Welcome back Finedon Road Yard |magazine = [[Rail Express]] |issue = 122 |date = July 2006 |page = 3}}</ref> During March 2007, First GBRf commenced operating its first coal trains, on behalf of both [[Drax Group]] and [[EDF Energy]].<ref>{{cite magazine |title = GBRF wins first coal contract |magazine = [[Today's Railways UK]] |issue = 54 |date = July 2006 |page = 15}}</ref><ref>{{cite magazine |title = GB Railfreight expands into coal |magazine = [[Rail Express]] |issue = 122 |date = July 2006 |page = 7}}</ref><ref>{{cite magazine |title = GBRf enters coal market |magazine = [[The Railway Magazine]] |issue = 1264 |date = August 2006 |page = 6}}</ref><ref>{{cite magazine |title = GBRf aims to be first for freight |magazine = [[Rail Magazine]] |issue = 603 |date = 22 October 2008 |pages = 38–42}}</ref>

In June 2007, the business was renamed First GBRf.<ref>{{cite magazine |title = More new locos and wagons ordered as GB Railfreight becomes FirstGBRf |magazine = [[Rail Express]]|issue = 134 |date = July 2007 |page = 7}}</ref><ref>{{cite magazine |title = GB Railfreight becomes FirstGBRf |magazine = [[The Railway Magazine]] |issue = 1276 |date = August 2007 |page = 76}}</ref>

During summer 2009, First GBRf was granted a passenger licence, allowing it to operate [[charter]] services.<ref>{{cite magazine |title = GBRf expands operations with charter trips |magazine = [[Rail Magazine]]|issue = 645 |date = 2 June 2010 |page = 34}}</ref> Between December 2009 and July 2010, First GBRf operated passenger services under contract to the train operating company [[First Great Western]]. These services, running from [[Cardiff Central railway station|Cardiff Central]] to [[Taunton railway station|Taunton]], consisted of hired [[Virgin Trains]] [[British Rail Class 57|Class 57/3]] locomotives hauling rakes of [[British Rail Mark 2|Mark 2]] carriages.<ref>{{cite web |url = http://www.tauntontrains.co.uk/LOCOHAULED.htm |title = First Great Western |publisher = tauntontrains.co.uk |access-date = 3 September 2014 |archive-date = 12 October 2012 |archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20121012074406/http://www.tauntontrains.co.uk/LOCOHAULED.htm |url-status = dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.tauntontrains.co.uk/LOCOHAULED.htm |title=WWW.TAUNTONTRAINS.CO.UK – LOCO HAULED |access-date=3 September 2014 |archive-date=12 October 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121012074406/http://www.tauntontrains.co.uk/LOCOHAULED.htm |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite magazine |title = First GBRf takes over on FGW Taunton diagram |magazine = [[Rail Express]] |issue = 164 |date = January 2010 |page = 7}}</ref><ref>{{cite magazine |title = First GBRf to operate FGW contract |magazine = [[The Railway Magazine]]|issue = 1306 |date = February 2010 |page = 61}}</ref>

===Europorte era===
[[File:GB Railfreight Europorte logo.svg|thumb|Logo while under [[Europorte]] ownership]]
During May 2010, FirstGroup announced that it was putting the business up for sale; various companies, including [[Europorte]], Freightliner and [[SNCF]], were reportedly interested in acquiring First GBRf.<ref>{{cite journal |url = http://www.joc.com/rail-intermodal/european-rivals-bid-gb-railfreight |title = European Rivals Bid for GB Railfreight |journal = The Journal of Commerce |first = Bruce |last = Barnard |date = 3 May 2010 |access-date = 18 October 2012 |archive-date = 6 May 2010 |archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20100506040400/http://www.joc.com/rail-intermodal/european-rivals-bid-gb-railfreight |url-status = dead }}</ref> On 1 June 2010, it was announced that it had been purchased by Europorte.<ref>{{cite magazine |url = http://www.railwaygazette.com/news/single-view/view/eurotunnel-buys-gb-railfreight-from-firstgroup.html |title = Eurotunnel buys GB Railfreight from FirstGroup |magazine = [[Railway Gazette International]] |date = 1 June 2010 |access-date = 18 October 2012 |archive-date = 6 June 2016 |archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20160606113843/http://www.railwaygazette.com/news/single-view/view/eurotunnel-buys-gb-railfreight-from-firstgroup.html |url-status = dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite magazine |title = Eurotunnel buys GBRf |magazine = [[The Railway Magazine]] |issue = 1312 |date = August 2010 |page = 10}}</ref> Following the acquisition by Europorte, the company reverted to its original name and a revised version of the original livery.

In February 2011, GBRf commenced operation of rail traffic at [[Cardiff]] Tidal/Tremorfa Works.<ref name="bray-tidal-sidings">{{cite web |title = Cardiff Tidal Sidings |date = 14 December 2011 |url = http://www.martinbray-ukloco.com/tidalsidings.html |work = Tidal, Margam & Canton |first = Martin |last = Bray |access-date = 18 October 2012 |archive-date = 3 September 2012 |archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20120903034903/http://www.martinbray-ukloco.com/tidalsidings.html |url-status = dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite magazine |title = GB Railfreight takes over at Cardiff Tidal Yard |magazine = [[Rail Express]] |issue = 179 |date = April 2011 |page = 50}}</ref> In 2012, GBRf commenced a ten-year contract to operate the {{convert|43|mi|adj=on}} rail network at Sahavirirya Steel Industries [[Lackenby]] steelworks, [[Teesside]].<ref name=RailwayMagazine1329>{{cite magazine |title = GBRf buys Norwegian locos for steelworks |magazine = [[The Railway Magazine]] |issue = 1329 |date = January 2012 |page = 85}}</ref>

During 2013, GB Railfreight were contracted to deliver [[British Rail Class 700|Class 700]] EMUs, constructed by [[Siemens Mobility|Siemens]] in [[Krefeld]], [[Germany]], from the Channel Tunnel; the firm was also contracted to haul [[British Rail Class 800|Class 800]]/[[British Rail Class 801|801s]] high speed trains. For the latter contract, GBRf provided trains crews during the testing process, as well as hauling the sets.<ref>{{cite magazine |title = GBRf wins IEP test contract for Class 800/801 trains |magazine = [[The Railway Magazine]] |issue = 1351 |date = November 2013 |page = 80}}</ref><ref>{{cite magazine |title = IEP trains to undergo night testing on East Coast line |magazine = [[Rail Magazine]]|issue = 738 |date = 25 December 2013 |page = 16}}</ref>

In April 2015, GB Railfreight commenced a contract from [[Serco]] to haul the ''[[Caledonian Sleeper]]''. [[British Rail Class 92|Class 92s]] haul it from [[Euston railway station|London Euston]] to [[Edinburgh Waverley railway station|Edinburgh Waverley]]/[[Glasgow Central railway station|Glasgow Central]] with rebuilt [[British Rail Class 73|Class 73/9s]] to haul it from Edinburgh to [[Aberdeen railway station|Aberdeen]], [[Inverness railway station|Inverness]] and [[Fort William railway station|Fort William]].<ref>{{cite magazine |title = The Sleepers are stirring |magazine = [[Rail Magazine]] |issue = 756 |date = 3 September 2014 |page = 70}}</ref> During early 2019, GBRf worked closely with [[Wabtec]] and Serco to prepare for the launch of the new [[British Rail Mark 5|Mark 5]] carriages for the Caledonian Sleeper.<ref>{{cite news |url = https://www.railadvent.co.uk/2019/04/gb-railfreight-help-launch-new-caledonian-sleeper-carriages.html |title = GB Railfreight help launch new Caledonian Sleeper carriages |publisher = RailAdvent|first = Michael |last = Holden |date = 25 April 2019}}</ref>

In October 2016, the business was purchased by the global investment firm [[EQT AB]], after which its operations were aligned with its [[Hector Rail]] subsidiary internationally.<ref>{{cite magazine |url = http://www.railwaygazette.com/news/freight/single-view/view/eqt-completes-acquisition-of-gb-railfreight.html |title = EQT completes acquisition of GB Railfreight |magazine = [[Railway Gazette International]] |date = 16 November 2016 |access-date = 18 July 2017 |archive-date = 29 July 2017 |archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20170729121855/http://www.railwaygazette.com/news/freight/single-view/view/eqt-completes-acquisition-of-gb-railfreight.html |url-status = dead }}</ref> At the time of the acquisition, GB Railfreight reportedly operated in excess of 1,000 trainloads of freight per week, moving roughly 15% of the UK’s rail freight, and had a forecast annual revenue of £125 million.<ref>{{cite web |url = https://www.automotivelogistics.media/private-equity-group-eqt-makes-offer-for-gb-railfreight/16701.article |title = Private equity group EQT makes offer for GB Railfreight |publisher = automotivelogistics.media |first = Gareth |last = Tredway |work = Automotive Logistics |date = 19 October 2016}}</ref>

During September 2019, EQT AB announced it had agreed to sell GB Railfreight to another investment company, [[M&G|Infracapital]]; the transaction was completed one month later.<ref>{{cite magazine |url = https://www.railwaygazette.com/uk/hector-rail-sells-gb-railfreight-to-infracapital/54636.article |title = Hector Rail sells GB Railfreight to Infracapital |magazine = Railway Gazette International |date = 23 September 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190923122609/https://www.railwaygazette.com/uk/hector-rail-sells-gb-railfreight-to-infracapital/54636.article |archive-date=23 September 2019 |url-status=dead}}</ref> At the time of the sale, GBRf was reportedly the third largest freight company operating in the UK, moving roughly 23% of all rail freight, had a turnover of more than £200 million per year and had in excess of 900 employees.<ref>{{cite web |url = https://www.multimodal.org.uk/article/new-owner-gb-railfreight |title = Another rail company changes hands |work = MultiModal UK |date = 23 September 2019 |publisher = multimodal.org.uk |access-date = 31 May 2022}}</ref>

On 9 April 2021, GBRf opened their new office in [[Peterborough]];<ref>{{cite news |date = 30 April 2021 |title = New Peterborough office for GB Railfreight officially opened |url = https://www.railadvent.co.uk/2021/04/new-peterborough-office-for-gb-railfreight-officially-opened.html |access-date = 3 May 2021 |work = RailAdvent}}</ref> the building houses the company's Operations departments, its 24-hour control centre, and undertakes training using onsite simulators; in the latter aspect, there are ambitions to become a major provider of training for train drivers and managers across the whole rail sector.<ref>{{cite web |url = https://news.railbusinessdaily.com/gb-railfreight-open-new-peterborough-office-to-kickstart-next-chapter/ |title = GB Railfreight open new Peterborough office to kickstart next chapter |publisher = railbusinessdaily.com |first = Danny |last = Longhorn |date = 30 April 2021}}</ref>

[[File:Tonbridge West Yard, Tonbridge, Kent 03.jpg|thumb|right|The new GBRf maintenance facility at Tonbridge West Yard, opened in September 2024|alt= Two diesel locomotives, behind which is a large blue building with "GB Railfreight" on the side]]
In September 2024, GBRf opened a new maintenance facility for its Class 66, [[British Rail Class 69|Class 69]] and Class 73 locomotives at its site in [[Tonbridge]], [[Kent]].<ref>{{cite magazine |title= GBRf opens new maintenance facility in Tonbridge |date= 2 September 2024 |magazine= [[Rail Magazine]] |url= https://www.railmagazine.com/news/2024/09/02/gbrf-opens-new-maintenance-facility-in-tonbridge |access-date= 9 September 2024 }}</ref>

==Fleet==
===Mainline fleet===
To commence operations, seven [[British Rail Class 66|Class 66/7s]] were ordered by GB Railfreight in April 2000.<ref>{{cite magazine |title = GB Railways Class 66s |magazine = [[The Railway Magazine]] |issue = 1188 |date = April 2000 |page = 11}}</ref> The type proved its value to the company, leading to multiple follow-on orders being placed. During October 2012, three unused Class 66s, previously ordered by Crossrail Benelux and stabled in the Netherlands, were purchased and transported to Britain by GBRf.<ref>{{cite magazine |title = GBRf to Bring Trio of Euro 66s to Britain |magazine = [[The Railway Magazine]] |issue = 1340 |date = December 2012 |page = 11}}</ref> In the following year, a further two Class 66s that had previously operated in continental Europe were also obtained. These were numbered 66747 to 66751 in the GBRf fleet.{{citation needed|date=May 2022}} By the end of 2014, the total number of Class 66s purchased by GBRf had risen to 72.<ref>{{cite magazine |title = GBRf welcomes the first five of 21 new 66s onto UK soil |magazine = [[Rail Magazine]] |issue = 753 |date = 23 July 2014 |page = 28}}</ref>

In 2015, it was confirmed a further seven Class 66s would be purchased. Even though the locomotive type no longer conforms with emissions regulations, GBRf had purchased some spare [[EMD 710]] engines, shipped them to the United Kingdom before the 31 December 2014 deadline and then returned them to the United States for fitting to the new locomotives to be delivered in 2016.<ref>{{cite magazine |title = More Class 66s for GB Railfreight to arrive next year? |magazine = [[Rail Magazine]]|issue = 764 |date = 24 December 2014 |page = 15}}</ref><ref>{{cite magazine |title = Loophole sees GBRf order another seven 66s |magazine = [[Today's Railways UK]]|issue = 158 |date = February 2015 |page = 54}}</ref> During late 2017, DB Cargo UK sold ten Class 66/0s (66008/016/046/058/081/132/141/184/238/250) to GBRf, who allocated the 66780–789 series to them in ascending order. 66789 (formerly 66250), was outshopped in [[British Rail]] Large Logo Blue and named ''British Rail 1948 – 1997'' to commemorate British Rail's 70th anniversary. It also acquired three [[British Rail Class 47#Class 47/7|Class 47/7s]] from [[Colas Rail]], for use on Caledonian Sleeper and stock move duties (47727, 47739, 47749)<ref>{{cite magazine |url = https://www.railmagazine.com/news/fleet/gb-railfreight-buys-three-class-47s |title = GB Railfreight buys three Class 47s |magazine = [[Rail Magazine]]|access-date = 5 June 2019}}</ref>

In June 2019, GBRf secured the lease of three Class 66 locomotives from [[Beacon Rail]] that had previously been in use with [[Hector Rail]] in Sweden as T66 403–405.<ref>{{cite magazine |title = GBRf takes delivery of Swedish Class 66 |magazine = [[Rail Magazine]]|issue = 881 |date = 19 June 2019 |page = 33}}</ref><ref>{{cite magazine |title = Three Hector Rail Class T66s to be moved to UK |magazine = [[Today's Railways Europe]] |issue = 284 |date = August 2019 |page = 40}}</ref> The first locomotive, 66790 (T66 403) arrived on 3 June and was moved from [[Port of Immingham|Immingham Docks]] to [[Longport, Staffordshire|Longport]], where [[Electro-Motive Diesel]] were to convert it to UK standards before it entered traffic. The locomotives date from November 2002, and were bought by Beacon Rail from [[Eversholt Rail Group|HSBC Rail]] in 2009.<ref name="auto">{{cite magazine |url = https://www.railmagazine.com/news/fleet/first-of-three-swedish-66s-arrives-for-gb-railfreight |title = First of three Swedish '66s' arrives for GB Railfreight |magazine = [[Rail Magazine]]|access-date = 5 June 2019}}</ref> During October 2020, GB Railfreight commenced the lease of a further five Class 66s from Beacon Rail, all of which being imported from Germany. The first of this batch were planned to enter service in April 2021, receiving the numbers 66793–797.<ref>{{cite web |title = GB Railfreight agrees deal for five new Class 66 locos – Railcam UK |url = http://news.railcam.uk/index.php/2020/10/08/gb-railfreight-agrees-deal-for-five-new-class-66-locos/ |publisher = railcam.uk |access-date = 9 October 2020 |archive-date = 19 October 2021 |archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20211019124433/https://news.railcam.uk/index.php/2020/10/08/gb-railfreight-agrees-deal-for-five-new-class-66-locos/ |url-status = dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite magazine |title = GBRf to acquire five more Euro 66s |magazine = [[Rail Express]] |issue = 293 |date = October 2020 |page = 24}}</ref><ref>{{cite magazine |title = GBRf acquires five more European 66s |magazine = [[Railways Illustrated]]|date = October 2020 |page = 17}}</ref>

[[File:Tonbridge West Yard, Tonbridge, Kent 01.jpg|thumb|right|Three GBRf [[British Rail Class 73|Class 73s]] at Tonbridge West Yard]] 
In 2004, GB Railways purchased six former [[Gatwick Express]] Class 73s. After GBRf won a contract to operate [[Network Rail]] infrastructure trains in the south-east, four were overhauled by [[FM Rail|Fragonset Railways]].<ref>{{cite magazine |title = New lease of life for GB Railways Class 73s |magazine = [[The Railway Magazine]] |issue = 1236 |date = April 2004 |page = 67}}</ref> Two more were purchased from Loram UK,<ref>{{cite magazine |url = https://www.railmagazine.com/news/fleet/gb-railfreight-buys-more-locomotives |title = GB Railfreight buys more locomotives |magazine = [[Rail Magazine]]|access-date = 5 June 2019}}</ref> and additional Class 73s were located and purchased, some from preservation, to give a total fleet, {{as of |July 2018}}, of 24 locomotives. Of these, eleven were completely re-engineered between 2014 and 2015, being equipped with {{cvt|1600|hp|kW}} [[MTU Friedrichshafen|MTU]] diesel power units; five were dedicated to Network Rail infrastructure traffic in the south of England while the remaining six being transferred to Scotland for use on the diesel-hauled legs of the [[Caledonian Sleeper]] services.{{citation needed|date=May 2022}}

GB Railfreight has a fleet of 16 [[British Rail Class 92|Class 92]] electric locomotives acquired by Europorte prior to the purchase of GB Railfreight.<ref>{{cite magazine |title = GBRf spends £50m on new Class 66/7s and Class 92s |magazine = [[Rail Magazine]]|issue = 741 |date = 5 February 2014 |page = 6}}</ref>

In August 2014, GBRf purchased a single [[British Rail Class 59|Class 59]] locomotive from the Germany company Heavy Haul Power International.<ref name=GBRf19Aug14>{{cite web |url = http://www.gbrailfreight.com/media-centre/news-releases/ |title = GB Railfreight brings hardy 'Yeoman Highlander' back to the UK |publisher = GB Railfreight |date = 19 August 2014 |access-date = 24 August 2014 |archive-date = 29 August 2019 |archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20190829144039/http://www.gbrailfreight.com/media-centre/news-releases/ |url-status = dead }}</ref><ref name=RailExpress20Aug14>{{cite magazine |url = http://www.railexpress.co.uk/news/yeoman-highlander-to-return-to-uk |title = Yeoman Highlander to return to the UK |magazine = [[Rail Express]] |date = 20 August 2014 |access-date = 28 August 2014 |archive-date = 18 October 2014 |archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20141018204741/http://www.railexpress.co.uk/news/yeoman-highlander-to-return-to-uk |url-status = dead }}</ref> This locomotive had originally been purchased by the [[Foster Yeoman]] group (along with its sister locomotives 59001/002/004/005), these being the first privately owned locomotives to operate under British Rail.{{citation needed|date=November 2024}}

In June 2018, GBRf acquired 16 of the [[British Rail Class 56|Class 56]] locomotives owned by [[UK Rail Leasing]] (UKRL), together with various parts.<ref>{{cite magazine |url = https://www.railmagazine.com/news/fleet/gb-railfreight-buys-16-class-56s-from-uk-rail-leasing |title = GB Railfreight buys 16 Class 56s from UK Rail Leasing |magazine = [[Rail Magazine]]|access-date = 5 June 2019}}</ref> Most of these were subsequently re-engineered. The locomotives were previously owned by DB Cargo and subsequently hired to Fertis for high speed rail construction trains in France; after their return to the UK, they were acquired by UKRL during 2014 for spot hire. Only 56081, 56098 and 56104 had been made operational by UKRL, with the majority stored at Leicester depot.<ref>{{cite web |url = http://www.rail.co.uk/rail-news/2014/ukrl-launch/ |title = UK Rail Leasing launch Class 56 fleet back into main line service |website = www.rail.co.uk |access-date = 5 June 2019 |archive-date = 1 April 2019 |archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20190401163311/http://www.rail.co.uk/rail-news/2014/ukrl-launch/ |url-status = dead }}</ref>

In early 2022, 2 ex-[[Colas Rail]] [[British Rail Class 67|Class 67s]] joined the fleet.<ref name=":0">{{cite magazine |title=GBRf gains Colas Class 67s |magazine=[[The Railway Magazine]] |issue=1451 |date=February 2022}}</ref> A new fleet of 16 [[British Rail Class 69|Class 69]] locomotives, converted from Class 56s, were also being delivered in different liveries and brands. Furthermore, that same year, GB Railfreight ordered 30 new [[British Rail Class 99 |Class 99]] bi-mode locomotives for delivery in 2025; these are intended to replace its Class 66 fleet.<ref name=":1">{{cite magazine |url=https://www.modernrailways.com/article/gbrf-orders-30-stadler-class-99-bi-mode-locos |title=GBRf orders 30 Stadler Class 99 bi-mode locos |magazine=[[Modern Railways]]|date=29 April 2022 |access-date=10 November 2022}}</ref>

In June 2023, GBRf began leases on 57303, 57305, 57306 and 57310.<ref name=RE326>{{cite magazine |title=DRS reshuffles ahead of Class 37 and 57 departures |magazine=[[Rail Express]] |issue=326 |date=July 2023 |page=16}}</ref> They are used for Multiple Unit transfers, and have also operated as the power for passenger charter trains.{{citation needed|date=November 2024}}

In February 2026 GB Railfreight has confirmed various diesel locomotives it will offer for sale at auction in March. It’s part of a broader fleet renewal programme. The disposal encompasses a range of older diesel traction vehicles. Inspections are scheduled to take place in the coming weeks at several locations.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Walton |first=Simon |date=2026-02-26 |title=GB Railfreight confirms diesel auction |url=https://www.railfreight.com/business/2026/02/26/gb-railfreight-confirms-diesel-auction/ |access-date=2026-03-02 |website=RailFreight.com |language=en-US}}</ref>The decision to sell the locos is due to the staged introduction of 30 bi-mode Class 99 locomotives.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Locomotive Sales |url=https://www.gbrailfreight.com/locomotive-sales/ |access-date=2026-03-02 |website=GBRf |language=en-GB}}</ref> 

===Heritage diesels===
GBRf has also utilised a number of heritage diesel locomotives. [[British Rail Class 20|Class 20s]] are used on [[London Underground]] [[London Underground S7 and S8 Stock|S Stock]] moves between [[Derby Litchurch Lane Works]], [[Old Dalby Test Track]] and London Underground's [[Neasden Depot]]. It hires these from various owners, including [[Harry Needle Railroad Company]]. During mid-2014, five [[British Rail Class 47|Class 47s]] were hired from [[Riviera Trains]] for a short period.<ref>{{cite magazine |title = More Riviera Trains 47s lined up for GBRf duties |magazine = [[Rail Magazine]] |issue = 750 |date = 11 June 2014 |page = 28}}</ref><ref>{{cite magazine |title = Three 47s on hire to GBRf |magazine = [[Today's Railways UK]]|issue = 152 |date = August 2014 |page = 62}}</ref> In January 2019, GB Railfreight received a pair of [[British Rail Class 50|Class 50]] locomotives on loan from the Class 50 Alliance Preservation Group, with both locomotives (50 007 and 50 049) repainted into GBRf livery and returned to service in March 2019.<ref>{{cite magazine |title = GBRf to use repainted Class 50s for spot-hire work |magazine = [[Rail Magazine]]|issue = 871 |date = 30 January 2019 |page = 32}}</ref> In August 2024, both locomotives were returned to the [[Severn Valley Railway]].<ref>{{cite web |last=DW25 |date=10 August 2024 |title=Large Logo Duo Return |url=https://www.fiftyfund-alliance.co.uk/post/large-logo-duo-return |access-date=5 November 2024 |website=Fifty Fund Alliance}}</ref>

Occasionally, GBRf has hired preserved locomotives, such as the [[British Rail Class 55|Class 55 Deltic]] no. 55022 ''Royal Scots Grey'' and [[British Rail Class 52|Class 52 Western]] no. D1015 ''Western Champion''.<ref>{{cite magazine |title = Deltic joins GBRf fleet |magazine = [[The Railway Magazine]]|issue = 1322 |date = June 2011 |page = 9}}</ref><ref>{{cite magazine |title = GBRf hires Deltic to haul EMUs |magazine = [[Rail Magazine]]|issue = 722 |date = 15 May 2013 |page = 35}}</ref><ref>{{cite magazine |title = GBRf hires a Western to haul Midlands freight |magazine = [[The Railway Magazine]] |issue = 1353 |date = December 2013 |page = 7}}</ref><ref>{{cite magazine |title = First a Deltic, now a Western for GBRf |magazine = [[Today's Railways UK]]|issue = 145 |date = January 2014 |page = 61}}</ref><ref>{{cite magazine |title = D1015 to stay with GBRf |magazine = [[Railways Illustrated]] |date = February 2014 |page = 8}}</ref>

===Shunter fleet===
To operate services on the Lackenby steelworks, Teesside network, eight 1996{{ndash}}97-era [[Maschinenbau Kiel]] locomotives were purchased from [[Vy|Norwegian State Railways]]. They were classed as [[NSB Di8|Di8]].<ref name=RailwayMagazine1329/>

GB Railfreight operated a pair of refurbished [[Thomas Hill (manufacturer)#Vanguards|Vanguard]] 0-6-0DH locos (re-numbered DH50-1 and DH50-2) for shunting purposes at Tremorfa/Cardiff Tidal works.<ref>{{cite web |url = http://www.philt.org.uk/Industrial/Ind-DE/18143694_pp8Nm7/18/1689426780_ndhXkkF#!i=1689426780&k=ndhXkkF |title = Industrial Diesel & Electric Locomotives |first = Phil |last = Trotter |format = photo gallery annotation |access-date = 18 October 2012 |quote = GBRf's DH50-1 … to replace ageing class 08s here with reconditioned industrial locomotives; … as rebuild no. 9376 of 2011.}}</ref> In December 2016, these were returned to Hunslet in favour of Class 08s (08389, 08877, 08924) hired in from [[Harry Needle Railroad Company]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Shunter news |url=https://www.pressreader.com/uk/railways-illustrated/20210504/281943135748883?srsltid=AfmBOopwaenoPyW3Yfh-A7A_z781fY-MTJTrpbwLFVl1A4ceUFh8sGxY |access-date=10 December 2024 |via=PressReader}}</ref> 

In addition, GB Railfreight operate 2 Class 08s (08925 and 08934) and 2 Class 09s (09002 and 09009) at [[Whitemoor marshalling yard|Whitemoor]].

In August 2024, GB Railfreight announced it had acquired four [[Clayton Equipment Company|Clayton Equipment]] [[British Rail Class 18|Class 18]] Hybrid+ CBD90 shunt locomotives, leased from [[Beacon Rail]]. These are diesel-electric + battery [[Bo-Bo]] shunters with recharging of the batteries both through a three phase shore supply and through [[regenerative braking]]. The locomotives are also fitted with a [[European emission standards#Emission standards for non-road mobile machinery|EU Stage V]] emissions compliant diesel engine.<ref>{{cite web |last=Batey |first=Sam |date=9 August 2024 |title=GB Railfreight adds new electric shunters as part of decarbonisation drive |url=https://www.gbrailfreight.com/gb-railfreight-adds-new-electric-shunters-as-part-of-decarbonisation-drive/ |access-date=14 August 2024 |website=GBRf }}</ref> They are based at [[Whitemoor marshalling yards|Whitemoor]], Eastleigh, and [[Bescot Yard|Bescot]].<ref>{{cite magazine |last=Roden |first=Andy |date=16 August 2024 |title=GBRf acquires four Class 18 shunters |url=https://www.modernrailwaysinsight.com/view_article.asp?ID=8814 |access-date=16 August 2024 |magazine=Modern Railways |url-access=subscription}}</ref>

GB Railfreight (GBRf) is a rail freight company in the United Kingdom. As of 2022, it is owned by the global investment company Infracapital, itself a subsidiary of M&G plc, a UK investment group.
GB Railfreight was established in April 1999 as the rail freight operating subsidiary of the train operating company GB Railways. It was granted an operator's licence in June 2000, and started running Intermodal container trains in February 2002; the haulage of other freight traffic commenced later that year. GBRf acquired numerous Class 66 locomotives to haul its trains; another early type would be the Class 20 and Class 73 locomotives. In August 2003, GBRf, via its parent company GB Railways, was acquired by FirstGroup; it was later rebranded as First GBRf. In 2005, it began running services for Royal Mail and Metronet; two years later, First GBRf ran its first coal trains. In 2009, it was granted a passenger license, after which it operated such services under contract to First Great Western.
In June 2010, the company was acquired by Europorte, after which the GB Railfreight branding and livery were promptly reinstated. Following this purchase, it took on Europorte's fleet of Class 92 electric locomotives, as well as buying additional Class 66s and Class 56s amongst other types to expand its inventory as service volume rose. Contracts to haul new-build rolling stock for operators and operate rail traffic at multiple steelworks were awarded during the early 2010s; GBRf also begun operations on hauling the Caledonian Sleeper service in April 2015. During October 2016, the company was bought by EQT AB, and was partly integrated with Hector Rail. In September 2019, GBRf's ownership changed hands again, this time to Infracapitial.
